To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the martensitic transformation can be induced in austenitic stainless steels by applied stress alone.

the transformation of austenite to martensite in stainless steel is a stress-induced transformation, that the stress required to induce the transformation is independent of the plastic strain, that the transformation is not affected by the rate of loading and that the transformation is reversible.

(i) the stress required to induce martensite in austenitic stainless steels is not constant, but increases with increasing strain rate; (ii) the stress required is independent of the applied strain; (iii) the stress required increases linearly with the temperature of the austenite; and (iv) the stress required decreases with increasing stacking fault energy (SFE).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an understanding of the mechanisms of deformation induced martenite transformation in steels.
the martensitic transformation and the mechanical behavior of steels.
the martensitic phase transformation in stainless steel.

martensitic transformations in austenite can be driven either by applied stresses or by strain induced defects.
, for stainless steels, the martensite formation is induced by stress, and the plastic deformation only affects the kinetics.

the stress induced transformation is a more important mechanism than strain induced transformation.

, for the austenitic stainless steels, the martensitic transformation is stress induced, and that the effect of plastic strain is to increase the stress required to initiate the transformation, and to decrease the rate of the transformation at constant stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stress-induced martensite formation in stainless steels is a thermally activated process, and the activation energy for the process is in the range of 100–300 kJ/mol.
the transformation in austenite stainless steels can be driven by stress alone, with no need to invoke a strain induced mechanism.

, in the absence of a strong driving force for transformation, the nucleation of martensite in austenitic stainless steels is strongly strain induced, and the plastic strain is the main parameter governing the martensitic transformation.
